_comment: Routing plan for gps-lora (kicad-routing skill). Net classes and rules already live in gps-lora.kicad_pro / gps-lora.kicad_dru; this file records the intent and drives review_routing.py.
_fab_note: Lion Circuits, Bangalore. Board rules kept as set in the project: 0.2 mm track/space, 0.8/0.4 mm vias, 0.5 mm copper-to-edge.

stackup.notes: L1 F.Cu signals + GND pour; L2 (GND) solid ground, no traces; L3 (PWR) 3V3 plane with +5V island, no traces; L4 B.Cu signals + GND pour. Exact Lion Circuits stackup still pending.

netclasses.name: Power
netclasses._current_note: 0.75 A = polyfuse hold current, the most the input path can carry continuously; trace_width.py gives 0.30 mm recommended (external, 1 oz, 10 C).

netclasses.name: USB
netclasses._impedance_note: ESP32-S3 USB is full speed (12 Mbit/s): 90 ohm geometry is not critical at this edge rate. Width/gap are placeholders until the Lion stackup arrives.

netclasses.name: RF
netclasses._impedance_note: 50 ohm width pending the Lion stackup.

diff_pairs.name: USB
diff_pairs._note: Full-speed only; skew budget is generous. P and N could not share one channel past the microSD bus (see report).

critical_order: 1. Power path (VBUS -> F201 -> U202 -> +3V3 plane) - routed by the user
2. GNSS (U401) zone rules from kicad_dru: no signal vias within 20 mm, top layer only under the module
3. USB D+/D- connector -> USBLC6 -> R304/R305 -> IO20/IO19
4. SPI buses (microSD, LoRa) point-to-point over the In1 plane
5. Everything else; then GND pad vias, stitching (6 mm grid, 4 mm edge fence)
